items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: in there and work Wilcox and Sy and all of them with that six-part harmony.

ctx.x: Lunceford told me we have to teach him. Three weeks and you can lead the band, I didn't know you could lead anyway. Because there wasn't that much music. So they just started -- let him do a lot of solo work and then we don't have to worry too much, because you see, the guys wasn't writing good harmony in those days, not six-part. So I had to kind of get
in there and work Wilcox and Sy and all of them with that six-part harmony.
So that's how I got in Lunceford's band. And the reason I left Lunceford, because he never did get me no further than $60, $65 a week. And I joined Basie for $150.
